Hat Values for brma Objects

Source: R/hatvalues.R
hatvalues.brma.Rd

Computes hat values (leverages) from a fitted brma object. Returns posterior mean leverages, one for each observation.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'brma'
hatvalues(model, max_samples = Inf, ...)

Arguments

model

a fitted brma object

max_samples

maximum posterior draws used for known-V brma.mv() marginal covariance computations. Defaults to Inf. Finite values deterministically thin draws across posterior row order.

...

additional arguments (currently ignored)

Value

A numeric vector of length K, one posterior mean leverage per observation.

Details

Hat values (leverages) measure the influence of each observation on the fitted values. In a Bayesian meta-analysis, the random effects variance \(\tau^2\) is uncertain, so the hat matrix depends on the posterior samples of \(\tau^2\).

This function computes the diagonal elements of the hat matrix: $$h_i = (X (X^T W X)^{-1} X^T W)_{ii}$$ where \(W\) is the fitted precision matrix. Without additional likelihood weights it is the inverse marginal covariance; likelihood weights modify estimation precision without redefining the original outcome covariance used to standardize residuals.

The hat matrix is computed for each posterior draw and then averaged over draws, matching the vector output shape used by metafor. The members of a RoBMA() ensemble can differ in their PET and PEESE terms; each draw then uses the design of the member it belongs to (the location columns plus the PET column of PET members or the PEESE column of PEESE members), and the reported leverage is the posterior mean over all draws. For known-V brma.mv() random-formula models, leverages use the marginal GLS covariance \(V + ZGZ'\).

This method is available only for normal outcome models without weightfunction selection.

For known-V models, the leverages require applying the inverse of the marginal covariance. A covariance that is too ill-conditioned for that (a reciprocal condition number of about 2e-10 or less in any posterior draw used) is unavailable: the call stops with an error of class RoBMA_known_v_precision_unavailable, whose parent class is RoBMA_numerical_unavailable, instead of returning a rounded number. The condition carries the draw positions (rows) and their reciprocal_condition.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (requireNamespace("metadat", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(dat.bcg, package = "metadat")
  dat <- metafor::escalc(
    measure = "RR",
    ai      = tpos,
    bi      = tneg,
    ci      = cpos,
    di      = cneg,
    data    = dat.bcg
  )

  fit <- brma(yi = yi, vi = vi, data = dat, measure = "RR")
  hatvalues(fit)
}
} # }
